errors.quote: The permutations of [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) are never executed, since they cancel ([Retained permutation cancellation](retained-permutations.md)), so no row charges them.
errors.problem: In the paper only the source permutation R cancels, across the forward transforms, the pointwise product and the opposite-sign transform (Lemma lem:chirp-permutation). The target permutation Q does not cancel: Bluestein's chirp identity carries out its frequency change without applying Q as a separate permutation. The conclusion that no row charges them is right; the reason given for Q is wrong.

errors.quote: an exchange acts on chunks of only $K=\Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ bits and saves a factor $K^{-(1-\tau)}=p^{-\epsilon c(1-\tau)}$ against a full pass
errors.problem: One exchange costs O(VK^tau), more than a full pass O(V). The saving K^{1-tau} (multiplier K^{-(1-tau)}) is measured against moving the K bits with K plain passes, O(VK); over all O(p/K) exchanges that gives pK^{tau-1} against p. 'Against a full pass' names the wrong baseline.

errors.quote: With $\lg n=\max\{\lceil\log_2n\rceil,1\}$, within a constant factor of $\log n$ and at least $1$
errors.problem: At n = 1, log n = 0 while lg n = 1, so lg n is within a constant factor of log n only for n >= 2. That gap is the reason for the max with 1. The paper does not make this claim; it states the bound directly with lg n.
